title: Fleet mix capacity sensitivity playbook
summary: Playbook-style sensitivity analysis for mixed GPU fleet capacity planning under different quantization and batching regimes. Produces recommended fleet mix and short operational runbook for rollouts and fallback triggers.
content:
Sheet: Fleet mix capacity sensitivity

Overview:
This sheet captures a compact sensitivity matrix for regional fleet planning where we mix instance classes (A100/H100/RTX6XX), quantization profiles (fp16/int8/4-bit), and batching strategies (latency-targeted vs throughput-targeted). The goal is to map throughput gains to measured quality delta and provide runbook actions when utilization or quality drift cross thresholds.

Assumptions (applied across scenarios):
- Baseline model: opensource-llm-v2 (seq_len=1024 typical, median request tokens=80)
- Workload shape: 70% short (<64 tokens), 25% medium (64-256), 5% long (>256)
- Cost basis: normalized to $/token for A100 FP16 baseline = 1.0 unit
- KV cache hit assumed for 30% of repeated prefixes
- Target p95 latency SLOs: latency-tier-low=120ms, latency-tier-medium=350ms

Key metrics (columns used below):
- Region: region code (us-west/us-east/eu-central/ap-sg)
- Fleet mix: percent allocation to each GPU class (A100/H100/RTX)
- Quant: fp16 | int8 | 4bit-llm-int4 (operation profile)
- Batch mode: latency-window (max ms) or throughput (max batch size)
- Eff_throughput_rps: effective request/sec (average)
- p50_latency_ms: p50 end-to-end generation
- p95_latency_ms: p95 end-to-end generation
- Quality_delta_pts: delta compared to fp16 baseline (MOS-like), negative = quality drop
- Token_unit_cost_rel: relative cost per token versus baseline
- Utilization_pct: observed GPU utilization under steady load scenario (0-100)
- Notes: operational remarks and fallback triggers

Scenario table (selected subset from model runs / load tests):
Region | Fleet mix | Quant | Batch mode | Eff_throughput_rps | p50_latency_ms | p95_latency_ms | Quality_delta_pts | Token_unit_cost_rel | Utilization_pct | Notes
us-west | A100:70/H100:20/RTX:10 | fp16 | latency-window=80ms | 320 | 85 | 140 | 0.0 | 1.00 | 68 | baseline profile, p95 within SLO
us-west | A100:40/H100:50/RTX:10 | int8 | latency-window=120ms | 510 | 110 | 200 | -1.8 | 0.62 | 76 | cost savings significant; small MOS drop in long-turn prompts
us-west | A100:20/H100:70/RTX:10 | 4bit | throughput=batch=128 | 720 | 145 | 360 | -3.7 | 0.44 | 83 | p95 approaches medium SLO, recommend canary with fallback to int8

east | A100:60/H100:30/RTX:10 | fp16 | latency-window=100ms | 310 | 95 | 155 | 0.0 | 1.00 | 65 | steady
east | A100:30/H100:60/RTX:10 | int8 | throughput=batch=96 | 490 | 130 | 240 | -2.1 | 0.59 | 78 | note longer-tail increase for >256 tokens
east | A100:10/H100:80/RTX:10 | 4bit | throughput=batch=160 | 700 | 170 | 410 | -4.2 | 0.40 | 86 | high utilization, increased error rates observed in 0.5% of runs

eu | A100:80/H100:10/RTX:10 | fp16 | latency-window=80ms | 290 | 88 | 150 | 0.0 | 1.00 | 62 | conservative mix due to regional demand forecasting
eu | A100:45/H100:45/RTX:10 | int8 | latency-window=120ms | 480 | 120 | 220 | -1.5 | 0.65 | 73 | cost/throughput tradeoff matches SLA needs
eu | A100:20/H100:70/RTX:10 | 4bit | throughput=batch=128 | 690 | 160 | 385 | -3.9 | 0.42 | 82 | recommend staged rollout with quality monitors

ap-sg | A100:50/H100:40/RTX:10 | fp16 | latency-window=100ms | 270 | 105 | 190 | 0.0 | 1.00 | 60 | observed diurnal spikes CET->APAC
ap-sg | A100:20/H100:70/RTX:10 | int8 | throughput=batch=96 | 460 | 135 | 275 | -2.4 | 0.58 | 79 | runbook: scale H100 pool during morning window
ap-sg | A100:5/H100:85/RTX:10 | 4bit | throughput=batch=192 | 680 | 185 | 430 | -4.8 | 0.38 | 88 | caution: error burst during mem pressure events; increase retry budget

Capacity projection (monthly peak qps requirement = 1.2M req/day -> convert to sustained rps):
- Target 95th percentile sustained rps across regions: 650 aggregate (after caching and burst absorbed by autoscale).
- Fleet sizing guidance (safety buffer = 1.25x): for mixed int8 profile, plan aggregate capacity for 820 rps equivalent.

Sensitivity analysis summary (short):
- Moving from fp16->int8 typically reduces token_unit_cost_rel by ~35-40% while dropping MOS by ~1.5-2.5 pts in our eval set; p95 latency increases ~40-70ms depending on batching mode.
- Moving to 4-bit gives another ~25-30% cost reduction vs int8 but quality hit widens (~3.5-5 pts) and p95 latency often breaches medium SLO when batch sizes are large.
- Throughput-targeted batching (large batch size) amplifies effective throughput by ~1.3-1.8x but increases p95 tail; latency-window strategies keep p95 tighter at the cost of throughput.
- GPU mix: H100-heavy mixes give better cost-per-token in int8/4bit runs but increase utilization; A100-heavy mixes favor latency predictability. RTX-class used only for low-cost experimental burst capacity where quality sensitivity is low (e.g., rerank-only workloads).

Operational recommendations / rollout cookbook:
1) Canary plan: start int8 on 5% traffic routed to H100 pool (latency-window=120ms). Monitor: per-prompt MOS delta, p95 latency, error rate. 24h pass -> 25% -> 50% -> full region. Fallback: automatic route to A100 fp16 when p95 > 2x SLO or MOS delta < -3.0 for 1h.
2) 4-bit adoption: only for cost-constrained customers and non-critical workloads. Require A/B evals on customer prompt set and automated quality gating (delta threshold -3.0). Limit batch_size <= 128 for >50% long-tail traffic.
3) Autoscale hooks: when Utilization_pct > 80% for 10 consecutive minutes, spin up reserved burst capacity (RTX pool) and reduce batch window by 25% to reduce p95 tail.
4) Monitoring: add per-model prompt-set quality evaluation (rolling sample 1k inferences/day), create alert when avg quality delta < -2.5 over 3 hours.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Need more real-customer prompt sets from mid-market accounts to validate MOS deltas for int8/4bit over long sequences. (Owner: Priya)
- Verify memory-pressure-induced error burst on 4-bit H100 runs; schedule stress test with longer sequences (owner: Marcus).
- Economics: compute cross-region transfer costs when failing over to other regions (finance input needed).

Appendix: quick formula notes (for sheet formulas):
- Eff_throughput_rps = measured_tokens_per_second / avg_tokens_per_request
- Token_unit_cost_rel = (inference_time_ms * gpu_cost_rate) / baseline_norm_factor (normalized in our test harness)
- Utilization_pct = average_gpu_utilization_during_test * 100

Checklist before rollout:
- [ ] Canary job scheduled with dataset A (customer-sample)
- [ ] Quality evaluator runbook created and integrated into Redwood Optimize alerts
- [ ] Autoscale policy updated for burst RTX pool
- [ ] Customer communication template for potential quality drift

Notes to reviewers:
- This sheet is intentionally compact; the upstream sim workbook contains the full per-job traces. Use this for quick regional planning and playbook steps.
- Please review the fallback thresholds and MOS gate numbers; those were tuned on the internal eval set and may need customer-specific adjustments.

End of sheet.
